items.text: Mike Quigley has represented Illinois's 5th District in the U.S. House since 2009. He previously served on the Cook County Board of Commissioners and taught environmental policy at Loyola University Chicago. In the House, he sits on the Intelligence Committee and the Appropriations Committee, where he serves on the Transportation, Housing and Urban Development subcommittee. He co-chairs the Congressional Ukraine Caucus and founded the Transparency Caucus.

items.text: Quigley has said U.S. elections are secure and supported funding for equipment upgrades and poll worker training. He criticized the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, saying its requirements for proof of citizenship and photo IDs would make voting more difficult. In 2026, he co-introduced a bill to create a defense working group between the U.S. and Ukraine. He has called for the dismantling of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement in its current form.

items.text: In 2021, he announced his support for the Medicare for All Act. He co-led the 2026 House passage of a bill to reauthorize the 2021 ACT for ALS law, which funds research for neurodegenerative diseases. In 2026, he co-introduced legislation to nullify a rule that weakened Endangered Species Act protections. He has secured over $58 million in community project funding for his district, including CTA station upgrades and lead pipe replacement.
